Replace.Text: Bencomo (c. 1438-1494) was mencey of Taoro, the richest of the nine Guanche kingdoms of Tenerife, and the soul of the resistance to the Castilian conquest. In May 1494 his warriors ambushed Alonso Fernandez de Lugo's army in the ravine of Acentejo and destroyed it, the worst defeat the conquerors suffered in the Canaries.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]He fell in November of the same year at the battle of Aguere, when Lugo returned with a larger army. Tenerife, the last island to resist, submitted in 1496. The scenario places him a century early, as the embodiment of the Guanche menceys.

Bencomo, mencey of Taoro, the greatest of the nine kingdoms of Achinet. Your people climbed out of their caves to pasture goats under the white peak of Echeyde, where the evil one is chained and the sacred mountain smokes. Nine menceys share the island; none of them is your equal.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The island is large, the valleys of the north are green, and the summit belongs to the gods. Unite the menceyatos under Taoro, fill the ravines with herds and tagoror councils, and when strangers one day come out of the sea, let them learn what the Guanches did to the invaders at Acentejo.
Founded cities start with additional territory. Units receive +15% [ICON_STRENGTH] Combat Strength when fighting inside Guanche territory.

Bencomo, mencey of Taoro, the greatest of the nine kingdoms of Achinet. Your people climbed out of their caves to pasture goats under the white peak of Echeyde, where the evil one is chained and the sacred mountain smokes. Nine menceys share the island; none of them is your equal.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The island is large, the valleys of the north are green, and the summit belongs to the gods. Unite the menceyatos under Taoro, fill the ravines with herds and tagoror councils, and when strangers one day come out of the sea, let them learn what the Guanches did to the invaders at Acentejo.
You strike at Taoro? Every ravine on this island will fight you.
The menceys are united now. You did that.
Achaman sees this treachery. Prepare yourself.
You have chosen the ravines of Achinet for your grave. So be it.
The Guanches do not start wars. We finish them.
Taoro falls. Achinet does not forget.
You hold the valleys. You will never hold the mountain.
Our mummies will outlast your banners.
Pay, and the warriors stay home.
The menceyatos require a gift. Give it.
I am Bencomo, mencey of Taoro. You stand on Achinet, the island of Echeyde. State your purpose.
Welcome to Taoro. The mountain watches us both.
A stranger on the island. Speak, and speak truthfully.
The tagoror is in session. Speak.
The tagoror is in session. Speak.
Enough. Let the goats graze in peace.
No. That is not an exchange, that is a theft.
The island is ours again. Remember this.

Tenesor Semidan (died c. 1496) was the last guanarteme of Galdar, the northern kingdom of Gran Canaria. Captured in 1482 and taken to Castile, he was baptised as Fernando Guanarteme and returned to persuade his people to end a resistance that had lasted five years; he later fought beside the Castilians on Tenerife.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Pre-conquest Gran Canaria was the most stratified society of the islands: a king, a high priest, a council of nobles, collective granaries such as the Cenobio de Valeron and the painted cave of Galdar. The scenario borrows his name for the island's rulers a century earlier.

Tenesor Semidan, guanarteme of Agaldar, lord of the most populous and most ordered of the islands. Your people carve granaries into the cliffs, paint their caves in red and white, raise their dead on stone platforms and plant barley on terraces that climb to Roque Nublo, the sacred rock at the heart of Tamaran.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Telde in the east and Agaldar in the north have shared the island too long. Bring the faycan priests and the guayres under one guanarteme, build what no other island can build, and make the Canarii the people the archipelago is named after.

Tenesor Semidan, guanarteme of Agaldar, lord of the most populous and most ordered of the islands. Your people carve granaries into the cliffs, paint their caves in red and white, raise their dead on stone platforms and plant barley on terraces that climb to Roque Nublo, the sacred rock at the heart of Tamaran.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Telde in the east and Agaldar in the north have shared the island too long. Bring the faycan priests and the guayres under one guanarteme, build what no other island can build, and make the Canarii the people the archipelago is named after.
You attack the Canarii? The whole island rises against you.
Agaldar remembers insults for a long time.
So. The faycan warned me of you.
The guayres have decided. It is war.
Then the granaries will feed an army.
Tamaran falls. Spare the granaries; the people will need them.
You have the island. May it bring you as much joy as it brought me.
The caves will keep our paintings long after you are gone.
A gift for the guanarteme would be wise.
I am Tenesor Semidan, guanarteme of Agaldar, in the island of Tamaran. The Canarii welcome you.
You have reached Tamaran, the island of the Canarii. Speak.
A guest from across the water. Sit, and tell us of your island.
No. The Canarii are not fools.
The island is at peace again.

Tanausu (died 1493) was the chief of Acero, the canton of the Caldera de Taburiente on La Palma, and the last Benahoarita leader to resist the Castilians. He held the caldera against Alonso Fernandez de Lugo until he was taken by treachery during a truce in May 1493.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Shipped to Castile, he refused all food and died at sea. The Benahoaritas were goat-herding cave dwellers organised in twelve cantons; their name for the island, Benahoare, means 'my land'.

Tanausu, lord of Acero, the great caldera at the heart of Benahoare. Twelve cantons share the steepest island of the archipelago, and yours is the one nobody has ever taken: a fortress of cliffs and springs with a single entrance, where the Benahoaritas keep their herds and their freedom.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Your people are few and their island is a ladder of ravines. Make every ravine a wall, every spring a city, and let the bigger islands learn that numbers mean nothing on the slopes of the Caldera.
+20% [ICON_STRENGTH] Combat Strength against civilizations with more cities than you.

Tanausu, lord of Acero, the great caldera at the heart of Benahoare. Twelve cantons share the steepest island of the archipelago, and yours is the one nobody has ever taken: a fortress of cliffs and springs with a single entrance, where the Benahoaritas keep their herds and their freedom.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Your people are few and their island is a ladder of ravines. Make every ravine a wall, every spring a city, and let the bigger islands learn that numbers mean nothing on the slopes of the Caldera.
You attack Benahoare? Count your men now; you will not be able to later.
The cantons are one now. Thank yourself for that.
Come to the caldera, then. Nobody has left it alive.
War. The ravines will do the rest.
So be it. We have fought bigger.
You have taken the caldera. I will not eat your bread.
Benahoare is yours. The springs will outlive you.
You won by numbers. Remember that.
A gift would keep my warriors at home.
I am Tanausu, lord of Acero. You have found Benahoare. Few do.
Welcome to the island of ravines. Mind your step.
A stranger in the caldera. Speak quickly.
Go carefully. The paths are steep.
Go carefully. The paths are steep.

Hautacuperche (died 1488) was a Gomero of the canton of Mulagua who led the rebellion of 1488 against Hernan Peraza the Younger, the Castilian lord of La Gomera, killing him at the cave of Guahedum. The island had been nominally Castilian since the 1440s under a pact between the cantons and the Perazas.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The rising was crushed within weeks by Pedro de Vera; Hautacuperche died in the fighting and hundreds of Gomeros were executed or sold. The Gomeros' whistled language, the silbo, is still spoken on the island.

Hautacuperche, warrior of the canton of Mulagua on the round island of Gomera. Your people speak across the ravines with whistles, farm terraces cut into cliffs, and climb to Garajonay, the misty forest at the summit, to honour the ancestors.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Four cantons, Mulagua, Ipalan, Orone and Agana, share a small island with no flat ground at all. Make the ravines your roads, the terraces your wealth, and keep the whistled word of Gomera free of any lord from across the sea.
Units ignore terrain costs when moving into any tile with Hills. No maintenance costs for improvements in Hills; half elsewhere.

Hautacuperche, warrior of the canton of Mulagua on the round island of Gomera. Your people speak across the ravines with whistles, farm terraces cut into cliffs, and climb to Garajonay, the misty forest at the summit, to honour the ancestors.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Four cantons, Mulagua, Ipalan, Orone and Agana, share a small island with no flat ground at all. Make the ravines your roads, the terraces your wealth, and keep the whistled word of Gomera free of any lord from across the sea.
You attack Gomera? Every ravine already knows.
The cantons are warned. You will regret this.
Peraza thought the same. Ask him.
Then the whistles will carry a different message tonight.
War. You will not find us; we will find you.
Gomera falls. The whistles will go on without me.
You hold the island. You will never understand it.
Pay, and the whistles stay quiet.
I am Hautacuperche of Mulagua. You have reached Gomera, the island of the whistlers.
A visitor. The ravines told me you were coming.
Welcome. Speak, or whistle, we understand both.
May the mist hide your path.
May the mist hide your path.

Armiche was the king of El Hierro when Jean de Bethencourt's Normans arrived in 1405. Lured to a meeting by a Bimbache interpreter under promise of safe conduct, he and his people were seized and most were sold as slaves; the island was then settled by Normans and Castilians.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Bimbaches, perhaps a thousand people, lived from goats, shellfish and a little barley on an island without springs; the Garoe, a laurel tree on which the mist condensed, was their main water source and became the island's emblem.

Armiche, king of the Bimbaches on Esero, the smallest and westernmost of the islands, the last land before the edge of the world. Your people have no rivers; they drink the water that the sacred tree Garoe gathers from the clouds, and they guard it as the island's life.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Esero is small, but it is yours alone. Keep the Garoe green, keep the people together, and make the farthest island a place the gods remember.
+1 [ICON_PEACE] Faith in every city with an adjacent unimproved Forest tile; +2 with three or more.

Armiche, king of the Bimbaches on Esero, the smallest and westernmost of the islands, the last land before the edge of the world. Your people have no rivers; they drink the water that the sacred tree Garoe gathers from the clouds, and they guard it as the island's life.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Esero is small, but it is yours alone. Keep the Garoe green, keep the people together, and make the farthest island a place the gods remember.
You attack Esero? The gods of the tree will remember.
We are few, but we are all here.
Treachery. Esero has seen it before.
You would fight the Bimbaches? Then you will fight all of us.
War, then. The island is small; you will not get lost.
Esero falls. Guard the Garoe, or the island dies with us.
You hold the island. May the tree give you nothing.
The last island, the last to fall.
I am Armiche, king of Esero. You have sailed to the end of the world and found people here.
Welcome to Esero. The water is scarce; the welcome is not.
A stranger on the last island. Speak.
May the Garoe give you water.
May the Garoe give you water.

Guize was king of Maxorata, the northern of the two Majo kingdoms of Fuerteventura, at the time of Jean de Bethencourt's conquest. He and Ayoze, king of Jandia, submitted and were baptised in January 1405 after two years of raids and a famine; both kept a place in the Norman settlement.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Majos of Fuerteventura and Lanzarote were related peoples who lived from goats, barley and shellfish on the driest islands of the archipelago; the wall across the isthmus of La Pared that divided the two kingdoms gave the island its later Castilian name.
The Kingdoms of Maxorata and Jandia

Guize, king of Maxorata, the northern half of Erbania, the long dry island that the Majos divided with a wall from coast to coast. Your people are shepherds of goats on a land of sand and wind, where every well is a treasure and the sacred mountain Tindaya carries the footprints of the gods.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Ayoze rules Jandia beyond the wall. Unite the island, dig the wells, fill the plains with herds, and make the dry east of the archipelago the crossroads of its trade.
+3 [ICON_GOLD] Gold and +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture for each Trade Route with a different civilization. Trade Routes other civilizations send to you give +2 [ICON_GOLD] Gold to you and +1 to them.

Guize, king of Maxorata, the northern half of Erbania, the long dry island that the Majos divided with a wall from coast to coast. Your people are shepherds of goats on a land of sand and wind, where every well is a treasure and the sacred mountain Tindaya carries the footprints of the gods.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Ayoze rules Jandia beyond the wall. Unite the island, dig the wells, fill the plains with herds, and make the dry east of the archipelago the crossroads of its trade.
You attack the Majos? The island has swallowed better men.
Maxorata and Jandia stand together today. You did that.
Treachery in the dry season. We will remember.
Then the wall will have a new purpose.
War. The sand will cover your bones.
Erbania falls. The wind will erase you too.
You hold the island. Good luck finding water.
The Majos are shepherds. We will be here when you leave.
A gift for the king would be wise.
I am Guize, king of Maxorata. Erbania is dry, but its welcome is wide.
You have crossed to Erbania. Water first, then talk.
A stranger. Sit in the shade and speak.
Agreed. Trade is the breath of Erbania.

Guadarfia was king of Lanzarote when Jean de Bethencourt and Gadifer de La Salle landed in 1402. His people, perhaps three hundred after decades of slave raids, made a pact with the Normans; after a betrayal by Bethencourt's own men he rose against them, was defeated and baptised as Luis in 1404.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Lanzarote had been known to Europeans since Lancelotto Malocello's visit of about 1312, which gave the island its European name; its native name was Titerogaka. The royal seat was at Zonzamas, whose ruins survive near Teguise.

Guadarfia, king of Titerogaka, the first island that every ship from the north reaches. Your people live between the lava fields of the volcanoes and the sea, in a land where it almost never rains and where strangers have already come to take slaves more than once.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The sea brought the raiders; it can bring trade as well. Build harbours in every bay, fortify Zonzamas, and make Titerogaka the gate of the archipelago rather than its victim.
All coastal cities receive a free Harbor. Units may cross Mountains after the first Great General is earned, taking 50 HP damage if they end a turn on a Mountain.

Guadarfia, king of Titerogaka, the first island that every ship from the north reaches. Your people live between the lava fields of the volcanoes and the sea, in a land where it almost never rains and where strangers have already come to take slaves more than once.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The sea brought the raiders; it can bring trade as well. Build harbours in every bay, fortify Zonzamas, and make Titerogaka the gate of the archipelago rather than its victim.
You attack Titerogaka? We are used to it. We are also used to winning.
The harbours are closed to you now.
Treachery. Bethencourt would be proud of you.
Then the lava fields will have you.
War. We have fought raiders before.
Titerogaka falls. The sea will bring others after you.
You hold the island. The volcanoes hold you.
A gift for the harbour would be wise.
I am Guadarfia, king of Titerogaka. Ships reach my island first; so do the troubles. Which are you?
Welcome to Titerogaka. We have seen sails before.
A stranger from the sea. Speak plainly.
The Canary Islands in the year 1400. Seven islands, seven peoples, no boats. Build your island first; the sea comes later. Win by conquest.

The Beñesmen was the harvest festival of the Guanches, when the menceyatos set their quarrels aside, the gofio of the new barley was shared, and the strongest competed in wrestling and stick fighting. The guañameñe prophets and the councils of the tagoror gave the year its order.
[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Guañameñe[ENDCOLOR][NEWLINE][ICON_CULTURE] Culture cost of future Policies reduced by 10%.
[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Lucha[ENDCOLOR][NEWLINE]+1 [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness for each City in your empire.
[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Guatatiboa[ENDCOLOR][NEWLINE]+2 [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness from each different type of Luxury resource.

[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Pintaderas[ENDCOLOR] improves the cultural output of your empire allowing you to adopt more policies.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Adopting Pintaderas increases [ICON_CULTURE] Culture from Monuments and Temples by 2 each.

The islands had no metal and no writing, but they had art: the pintaderas, clay stamps of geometric pattern; the painted caves of Galdar; the spirals cut into the rock of La Palma; the tamarco cloaks of goat skin sewn with bone needles; the idol of Tara; the tajaraste dances of the feasts.
[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Tajaraste[ENDCOLOR][NEWLINE]Amount of [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness required to start a [ICON_GOLDEN_AGE] Golden Age reduced by 25%.
[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Tara[ENDCOLOR][NEWLINE]50% of excess [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness added each turn to the amount of [ICON_CULTURE] Culture that may be spent on Social Policies.
[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Harimaguadas[ENDCOLOR][NEWLINE]Increases [ICON_RESEARCH] Science output from Libraries and Observatories by 100%.

[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Guayres[ENDCOLOR] improves the effectiveness of one's army in a variety of ways.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Adopting Guayres gives +15 XP to all land combat units constructed from this point forward in the game.

The guayres and sigones were the warrior nobility of the islands, the menceyes their kings. Honor means warriors trained in the stone-throwing and stick-fighting of their youth, wounds dressed with the obsidian tabona, and the magado club that answered every landing on the beaches.
[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Menceyes[ENDCOLOR][NEWLINE]Rate at which Great Generals are born increased by 100%.
[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Tabona[ENDCOLOR][NEWLINE]Melee combat units gain the Medic promotion.
[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Magado[ENDCOLOR][NEWLINE]Gain [ICON_CULTURE] Culture for the empire equal to TRIPLE the [ICON_STRENGTH] Combat Strength of each enemy unit killed.
[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Guatimac[ENDCOLOR][NEWLINE]Rate at which [ICON_GREAT_PEOPLE] Great People are born increased by 100%.
[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Achamán[ENDCOLOR] increases the [ICON_PEACE] Faith of your people.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Adopting Achamán allows you to build Shrines and Temples in half the usual time.

Achamán was the sky god of Tenerife, Alcorac of Gran Canaria, Abora of La Palma; Magec the sun and Chaxiraxi the mother. The faycán and the harimaguadas kept the almogarén sanctuaries and the efequén temples, and in drought the whole people climbed to the baladero to make the goats bleat to the sky for rain.
[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Almogarén[ENDCOLOR][NEWLINE]20% discount on all purchases of religious units and buildings with [ICON_PEACE] Faith.
[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Faycán[ENDCOLOR][NEWLINE]Temples increase a city's [ICON_GOLD] Gold output by 25%.
[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Chaxiraxi[ENDCOLOR][NEWLINE]Cities with a majority religion also get the Pantheon belief bonus of the second most popular religion.
[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Baladero[ENDCOLOR][NEWLINE]If you founded a religion, gain a bonus Reformation belief.
[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Añepa[ENDCOLOR] provides bonuses to empires focused on [ICON_GOLD] Gold.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Adopting Añepa will boost [ICON_GOLD] Gold output in the [ICON_CAPITAL] Capital by 25%.

The añepa, the wooden sceptre of the mencey, stood for the tribute of the island: the goats of the guanil herds, the gánigo pots, the barley of the terraces. Nobles, the achimencey, and commoners, the achicaxna, each had their share in the guañac, the commonwealth of the valley.
[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Guanil[ENDCOLOR][NEWLINE]+2 [ICON_GOLD] Gold from all your land trade routes. Maintenance paid on Roads reduced by 50%.

[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Achimencey[ENDCOLOR][NEWLINE]Great Merchants are earned 25% faster. Receive double [ICON_GOLD] Gold from Great Merchant trade missions. +1 [ICON_MOVES] Movement for embarked units.
[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Guañac[ENDCOLOR][NEWLINE]Purchasing items in Cities requires 25% less [ICON_GOLD] Gold. +1 [ICON_RESEARCH] Science from every Mint and Market.

Guanche replacement for the Spearman. +1 [ICON_STRENGTH] Combat Strength and the Drill I promotion: +15% in rough terrain (hills, forest).
The Sigone is the Guanche Spearman: a little stronger, and at home in the ravines and hill slopes where the Guanches ambushed their enemies. Use it to hold rough ground and ravines.

The sigones were the captains of a Guanche mencey, nobles who led the warriors of a menceyato in war. The Guanche weapon was the banot, a fire-hardened wooden spear, used with a wooden shield (tarja) and backed by stones thrown with great accuracy; at Acentejo in 1494 the sigones of Taoro used the ravine to destroy a Castilian army.
Canarii replacement for the Archer. +1 [ICON_STRENGTH] Combat Strength and +1 [ICON_RANGE_STRENGTH] Ranged Combat Strength for the same cost.
The Tirador is the Canarii Archer: stronger at range and in defence, same price. Put it behind your Warriors and on hills, where its stones reach two tiles. It upgrades to the Composite Bowman.

Every chronicler of the conquest remarked on the Canarii's skill with thrown stones: they could hit a chosen target at a distance, parry stones in flight, and a volley from a hillside could stop an armoured column. Stone throwing was trained from childhood and was the first weapon of every island, but the Canarii of Gran Canaria were the acknowledged masters.
Benahoarita replacement for the Warrior. +1 [ICON_STRENGTH] Combat Strength and the Cover I promotion: +25% defence against ranged attacks.
The Magado is the Benahoarita Warrior: tougher, and hard to soften up with archers. It is the unit to garrison a ravine or a city with; it upgrades to the Swordsman.

The magado was the Benahoarita war club, a heavy wooden mace, and the name passed to the warriors who carried it. The Benahoaritas of La Palma were goat-herding cave dwellers who fought in the ravines of the steepest island of the archipelago; the caldera of Acero under Tanausu was never taken by assault.
Gomero replacement for the Scout. +1 [ICON_STRENGTH] Combat Strength and the Sentry promotion: +1 sight range.
The Silbador is the Gomero Scout: it sees one tile further and survives a little longer. Use it to map the island early and to watch the coast for landings.

The Gomeros spoke across the ravines of their island with the silbo, a whistled form of their language that carries for several kilometres. News of a landing, a raid or a council travelled from canton to canton faster than any runner; the silbo survived the conquest and is still taught on La Gomera.
Bimbache replacement for the Work Boat. Half the cost (25 [ICON_PRODUCTION]) and +1 [ICON_MOVES] Movement.
The Mariscador is the Bimbache Work Boat: cheap and quick. Build it early to improve every fish and shellfish tile around the small island; the sea feeds El Hierro.

The Bimbaches of El Hierro lived from goats, a little barley and the sea: their shell middens (concheros) line the coast of the island. On an island without springs, where water came from the mist on the Garoe tree, limpets, crabs and fish gathered from the rocks were a large part of every meal.
Majo replacement for the Spearman. 25% cheaper (42 [ICON_PRODUCTION]) and the Shock I promotion: +15% in open terrain.
The Ahepa is the Majo Spearman: cheap and strong on the open plains of Erbania. Field them in numbers.

The ahepa was the lance of the Majos of Fuerteventura, a long wooden spear with a fire-hardened point. The Majos fought on the open plains of the driest island of the archipelago, shepherd kingdoms divided by the wall of La Pared; their warriors also carried stones and the tezzeses, a fighting stick.
Majo replacement for the Warrior. The Amphibious promotion: no penalty when attacking from the sea or across a river.

The Guard of Zonzamas is the Majo Warrior of Lanzarote: the same strength, but it lands fighting. The unit for the first crossings to the next island once Optics allows embarkation; it upgrades to the Swordsman.

Zonzamas was the seat of the kings of Lanzarote, a walled complex near Teguise whose ruins survive. Lanzarote was the first island Europeans reached, and from the fourteenth century its people fought off slave raiders landing on their beaches; by 1402 the Majos of Guadarfia were a few hundred, hardened by a century of defending the shore.
Guanche replacement for the Monument. +1 [ICON_HAPPINESS_1] Happiness and no maintenance cost.
The Tagoror gives the culture of a Monument, a point of happiness and costs nothing to keep. Build it first in every city.

The tagoror was the council place of the Guanches: a ring of stones, with a larger seat for the mencey, where the nobles met to judge, to decide on war and to receive envoys. Every menceyato had one, and the word survives in place names across Tenerife.
Canarii replacement for the Granary. +3 [ICON_FOOD] Food instead of +2, and +1 [ICON_FOOD] Food from Sheep as well as Wheat, Bananas and Deer.
The Cenobio feeds a city faster than a Granary and turns the goat pastures of the hills into food. Build it early in every city that is to grow.

The Cenobio de Valeron on the north coast of Gran Canaria is a cliff honeycombed with more than three hundred chambers cut into the rock under a natural arch: the collective granary of the Canarii, where the harvest of the valley was stored under the guard of the harimaguadas. Similar fortified granaries exist across the island.
Benahoarita replacement for the Walls. +8 [ICON_STRENGTH] City Defense Strength instead of +5, +75 Hit Points instead of +50, no maintenance.
The Cuevas make a city much harder to take than ordinary Walls, for the same cost. With the Magado garrisoned behind them a Benahoarita city on a ravine is a fortress.

The peoples of the islands lived in caves, natural or cut into the volcanic tuff, and on La Palma the cave villages of the ravines of Aridane and Tedote climb the cliff faces in terraces. A cave settlement on a ledge, reached by one path, needed no wall; the conquerors had to take them one at a time.
Bimbache replacement for the Shrine. +2 [ICON_PEACE] Faith instead of +1, and +1 [ICON_FOOD] Food.
The Aranfaybo doubles the faith of a Shrine and feeds the city a little: rain is life on El Hierro. Build it early to found a pantheon before the bigger islands.

Aranfaybo was the spirit the Bimbaches invoked for rain: when the mist failed and the Garoe gave no water, the priests climbed to the cave of Asteheyta and called on it, and a pig-like creature was said to appear and bring the clouds. The rituals of the islands were almost all about water.
Majo replacement for the Circus. Does not require Horses or Ivory nearby, and gives +1 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production from Sheep.
The Gambuesa gives the two points of happiness of a Circus to any city, not only one with horses or ivory, and makes the goat pastures productive. Build it as the cities grow.

The gambuesa is the communal stone corral of Fuerteventura and Lanzarote, where the free-ranging goats of a whole district were driven once a year to be counted, marked and milked, a custom that outlived the conquest. The Majos were shepherds above all; the goat was food, clothing, leather and wealth.
Majo replacement for the Water Mill. Does not need a river, and costs 1 [ICON_GOLD] maintenance instead of 2.
There are no rivers in the islands, so nobody else can build a Water Mill: the Mareta gives Lanzarote +2 Food and +1 Production in every city, for half the upkeep.

The maretas of Lanzarote are rain cisterns: walled hollows and ponds that catch the run-off of the rare storms on an island with no springs. The Gran Mareta of Teguise watered the capital for centuries; the Majos of Zonzamas lived by the same art of catching every drop.
Bancales can only be built on hills and need no fresh water. Next to a mountain they provide additional food.

The bancales are the dry-stone terraces that climb the sides of the ravines of La Gomera, holding the thin volcanic soil on slopes too steep for any field. The Gomeros grew barley and beans on them, watered by channels from the springs of the laurel cloud forest of the summit, and the island is still ringed with their walls.

Бенкомо (ок. 1438-1494), менсей Таоро, богатейшего из девяти гуанчских королевств Тенерифе, и душа сопротивления кастильскому завоеванию. В мае 1494 года его воины устроили засаду армии Алонсо Фернандеса де Луго в ущелье Асентехо и уничтожили её: худшее поражение завоевателей на Канарах.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Он пал в ноябре того же года в битве при Агере, когда Луго вернулся с большей армией. Тенерифе, последний остров сопротивления, покорился в 1496 году. Сценарий ставит его на век раньше как воплощение гуанчских менсеев.

Бенкомо, менсей Таоро, величайшего из девяти королевств Ачинета. Твой народ вышел из пещер пасти коз под белой вершиной Эчейде, где прикован злой дух и курится священная гора. Девять менсеев делят остров; никто из них тебе не ровня.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Остров велик, долины севера зелены, а вершина принадлежит богам. Объедини менсейяты под Таоро, наполни ущелья стадами и советами тагорор, и когда однажды из моря придут чужаки, пусть узнают, что гуанчи сделали с захватчиками при Асентехо.
Основанные города получают дополнительную территорию. Юниты получают +15% [ICON_STRENGTH] боевой силы в сражениях на территории гуанчей.

Тенесор Семидан (ум. ок. 1496), последний гуанартеме Гальдара, северного королевства Гран-Канарии. Пленённый в 1482 году и увезённый в Кастилию, он был крещён как Фернандо Гуанартеме и вернулся, чтобы убедить свой народ прекратить сопротивление, длившееся пять лет; позже он воевал на стороне кастильцев на Тенерифе.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Гран-Канария до завоевания была самым расслоённым обществом островов: король, верховный жрец, совет знати, коллективные зернохранилища вроде Сенобио-де-Валерон и расписная пещера Гальдара. Сценарий берёт его имя для правителей острова веком раньше.

Тенесор Семидан, гуанартеме Агальдара, владыка самого населённого и самого упорядоченного из островов. Твой народ вырубает зернохранилища в скалах, расписывает пещеры красным и белым, кладёт своих мёртвых на каменные платформы и сеет ячмень на террасах, поднимающихся к Роке-Нубло, священной скале в сердце Тамарана.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Тельде на востоке и Агальдар на севере слишком долго делили остров. Собери жрецов-файканов и гуайров под одним гуанартеме, построй то, чего не может построить ни один другой остров, и сделай канариев народом, по которому назван весь архипелаг.

Танаусу (ум. 1493), вождь Асеро, кантона Кальдеры-де-Табурьенте на Ла-Пальме, последний из бенаоаритов, сопротивлявшийся кастильцам. Он удерживал кальдеру против Алонсо Фернандеса де Луго, пока не был схвачен предательски во время перемирия в мае 1493 года.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Отправленный в Кастилию, он отказался от пищи и умер в море. Бенаоариты были пещерными пастухами коз, жившими двенадцатью кантонами; их название острова, Бенаоаре, означает «моя земля».

Свистящий язык гомерцев, сильбо, на острове звучит до сих пор.

Армиче был королём Эль-Йерро, когда в 1405 году прибыли нормандцы Жана де Бетанкура. Гуадарфия был королём Лансароте, когда в 1402 году высадились Жан де Бетанкур и Гадифер де Ла Саль.
